utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Can we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As Your Honours please, my name is Niemann, I appear with my colleagues, Ms. McHenry, Mr. Turone and Mr. Huber for the prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: May we have appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I am Edina Residovic, Defence counsel for Mr. Zenjil Delalic. Mr. Delalic is also represented by Mr. Eugene O'Sullivan, professor from Canada, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I am Zeljko Olujic, Defence counsel for Mr. Mucic, along with my colleague Niko Duric, attorney from Croatia. I would also like to ask that my client not be present in the courtroom this afternoon because there will be a Catholic service in the detention unit this afternoon he would like to attend, so he asks for my permission to be excused today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That is not granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, my name is Karabdic, attorney from Sarajevo, Defence counsel for Mr. Hazim Delic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I am Cynthia McMurrey, along with my colleague, Ms. Nancy Boler. We represent Esad Landzo. --- Reporter not receiving translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we have some complaints. ---Pause in proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, you may proceed with your witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May I? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Residovic

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dzambasovic. Yesterday, before this chamber, you said that you have met Mr. Delalic again at the beginning of August, 1992, when you came with a specific task to the Mount Igman. Do you remember your statement before the chamber?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Dzambasovic, what is IKM Visoko, until that moment you were engaged with it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: This is a forward command post of the republican staff of Bosnia-Herzegovina. A part of officers which were unable to return to Sarajevo remained in the free territory and formed the so-called forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, sir, does that forward command post have authority on the basis of orders of the republican headquarters to issue orders and to appoint in the area of its authority?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: That forward command post had a role to propose appointments to the commander in chief and he would then appoint all the people to the vacant places and functions needed at the moment. So the commander in chief would appoint people for those important functions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the very day of yesterday -- at the very end of yesterday, excuse me, I have asked you what is your specific duty in Visoko when you came from Konjic? Were you a commander of a tactical group?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: And I have repeated yesterday, this was the process. This was yet another step in the organisation because we tried to organise tactical groups over the entire area due to operative reasons and needs. We formed a tactical group in Visoko, the commander of which was me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Brigadier, what was the reason for forming of TG-1 at that moment? What was the reason for its founding and what were its tasks?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: The reasons for formation of all tactical groups, including Tactical Group 1, were the same. That was, within a certain area, in a certain direction and a given period of time, to execute specific combat tasks. In this case, these were tasks connected to lifting of the blockade, like the siege of Sarajevo, for example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the same tasks given to Mr. Delalic, that is, the same tasks that the previous commander, Mustafa Polutak had?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Authorities and tasks of all TGs were the same. Specific tasks were different only in the respect because they refer to different territories, different areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, since, as a senior officer in that area, you performed your duties upon orders of the war presidency, was Mr. Delalic ever a commander of all the branches of armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina within a certain area or direction?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Military terminology do not know this terminology, all the branches, they're all the units and they have their names, numbers, et cetera. If you mean all the branches of the armed forces, this must be a mistake then or the lack of military terminology.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We believe that the transcript was misinterpreted because again we have the translation of branches instead of formations. We should have one term for all the military formations. I apologise, my colleague has asked me to pay attention to a detail. The witness had said, “according to the orders of superior command," and the interpretation said "war presidency," which is contrary to our aim. In order for us to examine the witnesses, those terms should be used in the same way in all the situations because it might influence the rulings of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (Microphone not on).

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I do not have an interpretation. There are technical difficulties. I believe I can hear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: About an ambiguity, so I was asking you whether that was a submission on the examination of your witness. Because you're examining your witness and you bring out only one through him. And you want to make a submission, there will be a background to it and we know that you are doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can be of assistance, the problem is one of interpretation and translation. The consistency of terms. That's the point. I am following the transcript and I was trying to convey to my colleague that there's inconsistency in the use of terms. As Judge Jan pointed out last week, "formations" is the correct word and we have "branches." We have "war presidency" instead of "supreme command." Those were the problems, Your Honour. And those are crucial terms in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We hear your observations. Go on with your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I ask now for the evidence, Prosecutor's evidence, 99 7/7 to be shown to the witness. Brigadier, before you you have an appointment signed by commander in chief, Sefir Halilovic, dated 27th of July, 1992, can you tell us whether you have seen this appointment earlier?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I have never seen it because it was not under my authority, although it -- there's a lack of logic in its formulation, but, nevertheless, I can see it was signed. Paragraph 1 of the appointment states that commander of all the formations of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the appointed person is Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have said it is illogical, can you explain to this chamber why do you think there's a lack of logic, what are all the formations of the armed forces? What were they at that time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: As soon as we had a decree with a force of law, the formations were consisted of HVO, MUP and TO. This is the reason. This is why all the formations is a surplus or illogical, which ever way we interpret it. The other thing, I can explain that through my example. A command of Tactical Group Visoko had only units from municipal staff, which were at that moment free of tasks. We could manoeuvre them, switch them from one task to another from one area to another. So tactical groups were consisted only from units which were -- which did not have designated tasks at given moments and those units were coming from municipal staffs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We all see these words on the paper. You have said that this is illogical. Can you tell us during 1992, was there at any time, Mr. Sefer Halilovic, who is commander in chief, was he ever a commander of all the formations, that is HVO, TO and MUP?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: According to the then organisation and structure, there was no possibility for him to be that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the superior authorities over HVO and who were over MUP?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: The superior authority of HVO was in Grude and the one for MUP was the ministry of the interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you look at this appointment again, can you tell us, were you able to implement it and practice, regardless to whom it refers to?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Unfortunately, this is only one of several illogical examples of orders. The circumstances were such that we did not have people with the expertise and there was no time to check out everybody. So in practice there were illogical orders. And we could spot them at all levels and they had to undergo certain changes for us to be able to implement them in practice. And in the army we say that an order that cannot be implemented is not an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, I will now show you another document. Can you please, Exhibit D-146/1 be shown to the witness. I have here copies for the chamber. Brigadier, do you have in your hands an order dated August 8th, 1992, signed president of the presidency Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I am looking at it, it is a little illegible, but I understand what it's saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this an order that appoints Zejnil Delalic as a commander of TG-1?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you read to us now paragraph 2 of the order?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: According to the military formation, this annuls the appointed commanders included in this order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A while ago you said that if in the case of illogical formulations in orders, which were such due to the lack of educated personnel, that you would try to remove such mistakes. Please tell us under paragraph 2 that you just read, was the previous order annulled by this new one? At least when we're talking about two different pieces of paper.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Regardless of what an order is, if we have a superior authority, as we have the president of the presidency here, then this means that. So I repeat, as soon as we have a superior signing an order, regardless of the type of an order, if it refers to the same person, a previous order is annulled. In this specific case, it means that an order issued earlier is being annulled and put out of force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, does this mean that the appointment dated July 27th, signed by commander in chief, Sefir Halilovic, even if it were valid, would have been annulled with this date, which was August 8th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Absolutely. This is a senior order concerning the function and the person signed it as well as the date of its issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that you were tasked with coming to Mount Igman where you were first supposed to coordinate activities there and then establish a temporary command for an operation which was upcoming at the time. Can you tell me what Tactical Groups were present in the area of Hadzici and Igman at the time when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: In the larger area of Mount Igman and Hadzici, there were two tactical groups. Tactical Group 1 and Tactical Group 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you also said that you proposed that in order to conduct the operation, a temporary command was to be established, did this take place, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, since we assessed the situation and found out it was very complex and the task, which was of strategic importance of us, which was lifting of the siege of Sarajevo, a temporary command, South or JUG was established on the basis of our proposal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like the witness to be shown D-145, Annex 6/8. It is on page 908 of Volume 3 of the military expert's report. Brigadier, is this a decision of 20 August 1992 signed by the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command, Sefik Halilovic, and president of presidency, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, and which establishes the temporary command JUG or south?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. This is the decision to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May this document please be returned into the file and that the witness be shown Exhibit 145, annex 6/9, which is the page 911, and may the witness also be given the English and the Bosnian versions, and the English one be placed on the ELMO. Brigadier, will you please review the Bosnian version of this appointment. Brigadier, did you in 1992 have an occasion to see this appointment?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I did. This is a proposal which was accepted and confirmed from both the staff of the Supreme Command and the president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please use the pointer and point at your position in the command. Can you tell us what was your duty at that time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: At that time I was the Chief of Staff of the temporary command of JUG, that is, I was deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you tell me whether Zejnil Delalic was appointed to this temporary command and what his duties were, if he was?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zejnil Delalic was appointed assistant for logistics for the very reasons which I mentioned yesterday, which was his ability -- his best qualification to become involved in those affairs, and at that time we had an acute lack of all the material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Beside the appointment to the temporary command JUG for assistant commander for logistics, did Zejnil Delalic remain commander of the Tactical Group 1, and if he did, in which area was he active at that time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: The very organisation of Tactical Groups was such that in carrying out important tasks, such as the one of the lifting of the siege of Sarajevo, these people or units could be used in other operations. Like here, the example is Mr. Delalic engaging in logistics for this operation. And another reason is that his Tactical Group was, as we put it in the military jargon, in an ancillary area. So that on that basis he was also able to be engaged in this affair, because there were unit commanders who had -- who would become commanders of these units in this ancillary --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are not getting transcript again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Are there any problems with the transcript? Make sure that they are corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am being told that it has been about five minutes that we have not had the questions and answers up appearing on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Continue for some time, see how we can go. If it's still a problem, I will rise and let them correct it. So carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, as far as I can see, neither questions or answer on either of these two documents have been taken down, so I am afraid that I will have to repeat all the questions in this area, because I believe that they are crucial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Do so. I don't see how crucial they were, but you may do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier -- Your Honours. A moment ago, Brigadier, you looked at the appointment of 20 August 1992 signed by the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command and the president of the presidency on the establishment of the temporary command JUG or south. You had this document in front of you, and can you please confirm that -- this is the previous one, the previous decision. Is this the decision of the temporary establishment of units for the operation JUG?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Even yesterday I pointed out that we assessed that two groups in such an important area cannot coordinate their activities, and on basis of this decision and the order which we saw later, a temporary group JUG was established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now Brigadier, will you please take a look at the appointment of 28 August 1992 signed by the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command and the president of presidency, and will you please tell me whether this appointment -- this document is the establishment of the temporary command JUG, which was referred to in the decision which you previously saw?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you tell me what was your duty in this temporary command?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I was the chief of staff and at the same time the deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Zejnil Delalic also appointed to this temporary command, and if he was, what was his duty?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, he was appointed assistant commander for logistics, because he was indeed best qualified for this job and we had a very desperate need for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I am going to ask you again the last question, which had not been taken down in the transcript originally. While he was engaged in the temporary command of JUG, was Mr. Delalic still commander of the Tactical Group 1, and where was the zone of activity of that Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. The previous appointments stayed in place. It was an ancillary area, Pazaric, Ormen, Hadzici, and all units in this ancillary area retained their commanders and commanding officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, at the time of the JUG operation, was the ancillary area at that time also the rear of the main force, and that was the area of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Just for your information, the defence of the City of Sarajevo was a circle. That is how it was organised. So that was the first ring of the defence. And the second ring was on the opposite side. So that this second ring went along the (inaudible) area which you have just mentioned, Bjelasnica (phoen), Kalinovik, Treskavica, Kalinovik, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, the witness has just recognised the appointment of 28th (sic), which includes his name as chief of staff, and it includes the name of Mr. Zejnil Delalic. This exhibit may not have been accepted as an authentic document, and now I would like to tender it as such. It was at 20 of August, not 28th August. It's 20th of August, for the transcript. Is this exhibit accepted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, it is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The preparations of the Operation JUG, immediately behind the defence lines in Sarajevo, were they such, in August and September of '92, that they required presence and involvement of all commanders?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: The process of preparations for combat operations is a very complex one, and professional soldiers know this. And, indeed, it was necessary to involve everyone who was taking part in this task. It involves all levels of command and control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, we probably do not need a very wide military explanation of all of this. I am asking you very specifically whether you and Zejnil Delalic both, as commander of the Tactical Group 1 and a member of the temporary command, did you physically spend all your time in this area?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. The system of command and control required this, and if it were otherwise, our being there would have been unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you remember, given the position which you had during this operation, in which area were the units from Konjic and Jablanica engaged at that time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: They were engaged in the main area or direction, in the area of responsibility of Tactical Group 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall, and I assume that as chief of staff you were engaged in preparation of all orders, which units and which forces of those units were under the command of the commander of Tactical Group 1 during this operation?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: These were forces from the units based in Tarcin and Pazaric, which were free, and I think that there were also part of units from Fojnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to the number of soldiers involved in these units which were commanded by Zejnil Delalic, did this formation have more soldiers than those which were under the command of Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: This question may be superfluous. These units always involve at least two-thirds of the total troops or soldiers that are used for this type of combat operation. This was an ancillary area. It would be logical that smaller troops, that is much smaller troops, would be involved there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, I would now like to move to another area of questioning. Can you tell me whether during this period it was usual that because of the main staff being under siege in Sarajevo that the staff would use its officers on the front line of the defence -- outside of defence for transmitting messages to other commanders in the area?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, of course, because the system of command and control had been interrupted. Had we had pigeons available to send messages, we would have used them, let alone commanders. In other words, we sort of made do any which way we found possible, regardless of whether this was part of any military doctrine or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, as a person who spent a substantial amount of time in this area, did you know whether in the area of Mount Igman there was a location which was secure enough, that is a location which was in constant operation where orders of the main staff of armed forces could be sent?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Orders could be sent to the command of the operative group, but in a manner that was not completely secure, that is, by telephone links. The fax communication and other types of communication did not exist. As an exception, we could use certain persons who would leave Sarajevo legally on some other business, mostly using international organisations which had the right to cross the runway and in some other ways.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, did this result in some orders not reaching the person to whom it was sent, and whether a subsequent order would sort of reach this person before the original one?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Unfortunately, this was a frequent case. As I have personal -- I can give you some examples from personal experience, and there were certain areas, such as Zepa, where certain orders issued to perform certain tasks could not reach that area for up to six months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can the witness now please be shown document D145 A/5/41, and it is on page 813. It is also part of the Prosecution Exhibit. It's part of the Prosecution Exhibit 99, but I don't know what the other number is. There are copies for the Court, so that we can all follow more easily the questions that I am about to ask. Brigadier, did you look at this document of 24 August 1992 signed by commander of TG-1, Mr. Zejnil Delalic? Can you please tell me, in light of the questions I asked of you previously, can you tell me what this is -- what this document refers to, just for -- I don't think you need to authenticate this document, it's already been admitted, but if you could just elucidate what the preamble of the document should mean for -- with respect to the person who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I believe that I have understood the purpose of your question. This is a classic example of transmission of an order of the superior command to the subordinate commands and formations. This is usual practice and this was a regular way of going about it. An order is always issued pursuant to something; in this case pursuant to an order of the supreme command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Brigadier. May -- the exhibit can be returned, and I would like to ask the Trial Chamber whether this would be a good convenient moment to -- oh, I apologise. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Still another half an hour 'til you get your coffee.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I do not need it. I just got confused by the time. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May the witness now please be shown document D145, annex -- Roman numeral V/42, and pages 818. It is also part of the Prosecution Exhibit Number 99. There are also sufficient number of copies for the Court. Brigadier, I presume you have never seen this document before. There's no need for you to authenticate it, but having in mind your previous answer, I thereby ask you, is this an order by the signing of which the commander transmitted as an order of the superior command or there's -- or is there something else in question? It seems like the transcript is out of order again. It has stopped again. I have been told that the transcript should continue with word, but it's not what I can see on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think it will be convenient for us to have a break at this stage and come back within 30 minutes, 25 to, while they work on the transcript and see how far they can go with it. So the Trial Chamber will now rise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DURIC
utterances.text: If I may beg Your Honours for a moment of your indulgence. Namely, on page 1 of today's record, Line 11, there has apparently has been a blank. Namely, my learned colleague, Mr. Olujic, has asked for Your Honours' permission for our client to attend mass, which will be held today on the premises of the detention unit at two o'clock this afternoon. Our client has also had waived his right to be present in this courtroom during the period of that hearing today. And also the introduction of today's appearance has not been recorded, so I most respectfully submit that this be rectified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If it has not been recorded, I repeat that I rejected the application because it conflicted with the presence of the accused person in the Trial Chamber during trials, so you will not be granted permission the to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. DURIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we understood that. But we would just like to add one little point on the same thing. Namely, that two days ago was one of the most important Catholic religious, you know, holidays and all the people who are Catholic will be attending the mass and we wanted to you know, do this on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You don't even know whether or not that I am Roman Catholic myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DURIC
utterances.text: Okay, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, before the break, I ask that you be shown the document, D-145, dated 28th of August, 1992. Did you have a chance to take a look at the document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the document under the date of the 28th of August, 1992, issued for the commander of the detention facility by Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Together with the document that I have already shown you, you have stated that, in that document, we deal with the transmission of an order of the supreme command staff. Can you give us an opinion on this order and tell us whether this is the same case or are we talking about something else?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: It is identical to the previous one. It concerns a transmission of an order of the supreme command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, even in the times of peace, when there are no conditions existing which you have explained before the chamber referring to the siege of Sarajevo, is it a custom in the military for commanders to transmit orders of superior command?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Orders of that type can be transmitted, particularly if there are just causes for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, in addition to the ability of a commander to transmit an order issued by his superior command, does the military practice know of a subordinated commander to receive from his superior command, a special task?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: It's happened. I can explain that through my personal example. I used to be chief of staff of first corps and, as my function, it was never stated that me as head of staff would go as head of delegation to Zepa to establish a protection area. But I was given such an order as a special task from my supreme command. And, in addition to that, I was in Zepa nine times until the protected area was established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If Mr. Delalic is a commander of TG-1 would receive an order that in addition to the tasks as a commander to perform another task, would this be a part of this common military practice and would he be obliged to perform it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: The military tries to avoid such orders, but in practice it does exist. Under our authority and a description of our functions there's always the last sentence which more or less goes as follows: A commanding officer, in addition to his function, also has to abide by the orders of his superiors, which are not contrary to the existing legislation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now ask that the witness be shown D-145, Annex 6/10, page 914 of the Bosnian text and 915 of the English text. Could you please place the English copy on the ELMO. Brigadier, does this appointment as a commander of a building refer to you personally?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. It refers to me. I was then a deputy commander, deputy head of the operation centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this another example of you as the head of the operation centre be given an additional task within a certain period of time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: It is an identical example as I have mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, is the special task that according to this document lasted for a certain period, did it in any way change your authorities and functions as the deputy head?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The exhibits may be returned to the files. Talking of duties of Mr. Delalic as a member of the temporary command JUG, you have pointed out that he was appointed assistant commander for logistics. In connection to that I ask for a document D-145, Annex 6/11 page 917 to be shown to the witness. Could you please place the English copy on the ELMO. Brigadier, are you looking at a document dated 28th of August, 1992, signed by the commander of TG-1, Delalic, Zejnil, is that the one?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the chamber you have described and Mr. Delalic was given authority in the temporary command JUG, but he also retained his authority as a commander of TG-1, could you tell us, was this request signed by Mr. Delalic in accordance with his authority?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, when such a request is taken by a deputy commander, or assistant commander, who then issues an order to the assistant commander to implement for the implementation of that particular task?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Requests and other acts which are not orders, may be sent in all direction, meaning horizontally and vertically however, depending on the need. In this case, a commander of municipal staff was given a task to issue an order to his assistant for logistics and he is the executor, meaning the commander who receives this request issues an order to his assistant for logistics, who is then his execution body and he has to implement the task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, you have said that you came to -- from Visoko, can you tell us under whose subordination the municipal staff of Visoko was at that time? What was its superior command?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Municipal staff were within the district staff and where the municipal staff was not functioning, they were directly connected to the republican staff of TO. Municipal staff of Visoko was directly subordinated to the staff of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you have spent a lot of time preparing the operation JUG in the municipality of Hadzici, do you know which staff was superior to the municipal staff of TO of Hadzici, Prozor and Taracin because this is all one municipal staff of Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Municipal staff of Hadzici and Trnovo, were under the regional staff in Sarajevo. Prozor was under the staff of Zenica. And around Neretva, Jablanica and Konjic. This part was somewhat specific because district staff of Mostar was not functioning. Those two staffs were directly under the republican staff. And there were several such cases, due to the circumstances during that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, at the time of operations for the lifting of the siege of Sarajevo, do you have any personal knowledge or experience of whether there were any obstructions on the part of the HVO in the conduct of operations?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Unfortunately, there were. In various ways and of various kinds. In the initial period we cooperated and we expected for that cooperation to be even better as time went on. And the initial period, little incidents started occurring.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us about that in brief because the chamber has already been told about it, but I just wanted to know whether you as the head of staff of a large operation during that period had any knowledge of such obstructions?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Obstructions were usually connected to the interceptions of convoys and ban of use of units and in certain areas that are under the authority of the HVO. Then the arrests began and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now ask you something that is separate from the topics of combat activities and authority. Prior to that I have an additional question. Do you know if Tactical Group 1 or Tactical Group 2 or your operative group at any moment had an authority over municipal staffs within their areas of activity?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: We had no authority over municipal staffs. To be more precise, we did not have an authority over the command of municipal staffs. But, we did have authority over units who came the us from municipal staffs to be engaged in this operation, in this task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, does the implementation of tasks of tactical groups and your temporary command, did it depend in any way upon the reception of information you had about your enemy?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This witness for Delalic. He's not a witness for himself. He's not standing trial. Much of the evidence we have heard concern his own performance and not related to the accused persons whose witness he is and for matters which have been testified.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness stated that every day at the beginning of August until the end of December was with Delalic and they were doing things together, so his knowledge of the responsibilities of tactical operational groups, a member of which was Mr. Delalic, and the temporary command, speak directly of Delalic's authority. I am not asking the witness to tell me what he was doing, but were duties and responsibilities of municipal staffs toward the tactical group and also, therefore, towards Zejnil Delalic. If he can know that from his experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I hear what he has been saying. He has been telling us what he has been doing in the affair of his own operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, did municipal staffs have an obligation to give information, intelligent information to commanders and command of tactical groups?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Within the system of control and command, every lower or subordinate command or unit is obliged to forward information to a superior unit. And each superior unit new information of importance for that unit are also obliged to forward to its superior command. So this was a two-way. When we go up in the hierarchy, these are notifications and if we go down -- strike that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- No translation.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: It is -- I don't know about --

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We didn't get some interpretation on the question and answer previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can the counsel please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: If I can be of assistance, on LiveNote, page 27, we are taking about the two-way transmission between the unit and the Tactical Group, and then the interpretation stops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The transcript continued, didn't it? Because I see the transcript continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The transcript continued, but the interpretation did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I just want to ask you whether in this Tactical Group there were bodies, either reconnaissance or intelligence bodies, which could have carried out these tasks for the Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: No. These were temporary formations and they only had bodies which were necessary for this specific task. In other words, they did not have bodies or other means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you know, from your own experience, from your involvement in the operations of which you spoke, do you know whether at that time there was some kind of an order from the main staff about the obligations of the municipal staffs to provide this type of operation -- of information to the Tactical Groups?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I did not see such orders, but I know that there were certain instructions which were drawn from certain rules, combat rules, and they related to intelligence activities. And these instructions and these rules were basically followed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was commander of Tactical Group, any Tactical Group, but in this particular case Mr. Zejnil Delalic, commander of Tactical Group 1, had a right to benefit from these instructions and could he base his requests on these instructions?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Of course. He was supposed to refer to these instructions, and as were -- was any other command. And there is no commander who can plan any combat operation if he does not have sufficient information on the enemy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If commander with his order encloses an order of supreme command, or another superior body, was he also supposed to refer to these rules?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: In this specific case, if there is an annex, if there is an enclosure, the preamble need not contain it, but it may. So, in other words, it is not an omission if it didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, let us move to another area. When you left Konjic, was there a prison there at that time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I do not know about prisons, and I have to state this with pleasure, that I never entered a prison, nor did I ever see one to date. And I do not know that there existed a prison in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sometime in August and September you worked with Zejnil Delalic on a daily basis. Did you ever hear or learn that Mr. Zejnil Delalic had any connection with the prison?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I did not hear that, and this would not have been part of any commanders responsibility, anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were prisons under the authority of the Tactical Group commanders?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: They were even less so, in terms of the commander of Tactical Groups' authority. They were under the authority of the MUP, and the MUP was the body that handled that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even though, as you just said, the Tactical Group had no authority over the prison, would a commander of the Tactical Group 1, regardless of who he was, could he appoint commander or guards or any other staff to a prison?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Within the framework of his responsibility, he could not do it. Now, whether somebody did it in reality is a completely different matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, did you -- have you ever heard -- did you ever hear that Mustufa Polutak, commander of Tactical Group 1, or Zejnil Delalic as another commander of TG-1, would appoint a commander of the Celebici prison; did you ever hear or learn about that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: No. And I did not pursue such information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, did you ever learn that the commander of the Celebici prison report to the commander of Tactical Group 1, regardless of whether this commander was Mustafa Polutak or Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: It would have made no sense, according to the rules, but what happened as reality, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In accordance with rules or based on your own knowledge, did you know of any report was sent to the Tactical Group 1 by either the municipal staff of Konjic or any other municipal staff, and would such a report be within the framework of responsibility of any Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I think I repeated this several times. It has nothing to do with responsibilities of any command, any Tactical Group, any formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Brigadier, I will now move onto another area. In the wartime, in the country which is engulfed in the war, many international organisations visit such places. As a ranking officer, could you tell me who gave permissions to various international organisations to visit different military facilities? Do you know this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: There were both orders and instructions in that regard, and the main staff was issuing permissions. And depending on the command or unit, they were obliged to accommodate any international organisation which had received permission to carry out a particular mission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you know what a practical -- what a Tactical Group does, both in terms of theory and practice, can you tell me whether Tactical Group 1 had authority to issue permissions for visits of international organisations to military facilities?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: They could have issued permissions if they had received such permission, either orally or in writing, from its own superior command. So they were -- they could have passed it on downward and issued it to whoever the visitor was in a given case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me now ask you a hypothetical question. If you as commander -- as chief of staff or commander of the temporary command were asked by an international organisation or Red Cross to mediate in order to obtain permission, would you be required to do that, would you have an obligation to do that according to your position?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I could have done it for humane or moral personal reasons. I could mediate it so that such permission could be obtained early, but nobody at a lower level could have done so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, you spoke very clearly about the only -- the subordinate units being under the command of the Tactical Group. Now, we are still in the same area here. Was commander of Tactical Group 1 -- had authority to punish the military personnel in the area of certain municipal staffs which were not subordinate directly to him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (Microphone not on) You already got information on that from so many witnesses, that those units who transferred TG-1, the commander of TG-1, would be able to punish them, not to the others. We have got it from so many witnesses. Why you get it duplicated, duplicated, the same information? The TG commander is responsible for the action of those units which have been placed under him, which have been seconded to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did discuss these issues. I just wanted to ask now whether, apart from that, he had any authority over other soldiers who were not directly subordinate or seconded to him.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Look, I believe that this issue should be clarified. Commander of the temporary command could not punish soldiers. They had their own home units. But he could send a file to -- a report to this unit so that this particular person could be prosecuted and punished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you are now referring to the soldiers who were subordinate to him; is that -- did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. He could -- he did not have a body who would be specially involved in this. Temporary formations arrived from their own home units, and if a person should be either punished or praised or decorated, for that matter, this would all be done in his home units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I think that you have clarified this issue. And what Judge Jan warned me about was regarding the other soldiers who were not subordinate to him, to whom they remained subordinate and who had the authority to punish them for any infractions or violations; in other words, all the other soldiers who were not subordinate to another command and who were not subordinate to the Tactical Groups. Under whose command, under whose authority did they remain? This has been stated several times, but my additional question to you now is who was in a position to punish soldiers who had remained within the municipal -- municipally-based units?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: These were the competent commanders of municipal staffs and later on commanders of brigades, divisions, depending on the stage of reorganisation of the armed forces that we were at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was commander of the Tactical Group 1 -- did the command of Tactical Group 1 have the same relation to all municipal staffs in its area of activity, such as the same relation to Jablanica, Hadzici and Konjic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. The status was the same. In other words, all municipal staffs had the same status in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Brigadier. Your Honours, this concludes my examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I just want to get this clarified. Tactical Group is a temporary formation for a certain particular purpose. Now, if a unit is placed under the command of the Tactical Group, would not the commander of the Tactical Group be able to punish for infringement of discipline, or would it have to send the person who has committed indiscipline to its parent unit?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, commander of the Tactical Group 1 could do this if the Tactical Group was such as we had, like in operations group JUG, which was isolated, and he had no other way of doing it. This we had in cases of Zepa, Srebrenica and such. That's where he could do this. But in the areas where the officer or soldier could go back to his home or parent unit, that is what would be normally done. So, in other words, we had both types of cases, but you are right, commander of the Tactical Group 1 could do this, but only in the case where the soldier had the ability to go back to his home base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Cross-examination. Cross-examined by Mr. Olujic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Dzambasovic.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am Mr. Zeljko Olujic, defence counsel for Mr. Zdravko Mucic. I have very few questions for you. In fact, I only have two questions for you. Firstly, Mr. Dzambasovic, can we say that you, as -- for a professional officer "in tempore criminus suspecte," that is in May of 1992, the Territorial Defence was not sufficiently armed and organised at a time of the aggression and attack against the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. We could -- I could confirm that partially. That is, the Territorial Defence was unarmed at the time when the aggression took place. In this period, and I had an opportunity to see that the HVO units were much better armed, but in terms of functioning of the system of command and control at lower levels, such as municipal staffs, that functioning was very good, and I was quite pleased with how it functioned in Konjic, especially since a joint hub command had been established. And, in fact, I wished personally that this would -- this establishment would go on and that the organisation would be strengthened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question, Mr. Dzambasovic. During your examination-in-chief you stated that sometime around 21 May you left Konjic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I believe so. I think it was a representative of the HVO who went with me. I gave you two dates, and I am not sure -- I just can't remember the HVO's representative's name, Azinovic or Petrovic. They may be able to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, did somebody come to replace you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Nobody came to replace me in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: May it please the Court. May I proceed? I only have several questions Cross-examined by Mr. Karabdic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, I am Salih Karabdic, defence counsel for Mr. Hazim Delic. I have several questions for you. You came to Konjic as member of the republican staff, the staff of the supreme command. In this position did you issue orders or could you issue orders to the military formations and other formations of the armed forces which -- of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I could not order, and not only myself, but nobody who was in this position and who had a role that I had. However, I was -- what I could do was to assess the situation and suggest what specifically could be done in this area, to notify the supreme command, and on the basis of that they could issue an order which would then be binding for this particular staff or command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you as a member of the staff did not have the right to issue orders or to issue commands? Did other members of the staff, deputies and assistants, have the right to order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (Microphone turned off) Deputies and assistants belonging to his delegation or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You are talking about deputies and assistants. Deputies or assistants belonging to his delegation or to somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: I was referring to his staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: His evidence seems to be as an adviser or as an observer, and he said he could not issue any orders. So this question does not really arise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honours. My question was only whether the other members from -- of the staff from which he came had the same authority and the same position, including all the assistants and deputies. That was the only purpose of the question.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: The right to command an order has other commander exclusively, that is his and his -- that is his authority and his only. This is the case in all armies of the world, and it is not for not if when you hear the comment. If something is working in a unit, everybody shares in the praise. If something goes wrong, it is only the commander's fault.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So according to these military rules, the commander is exclusively responsible for his unit? Is it only the commander who is responsible for his unit and to what extent is he responsible for his unit?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: The commander is always responsible for his unit, whether he is on vacation or wherever. He is always responsible for his unit. But he himself is -- he has to be responsible to his own superior, all the way up the chain of command, from the laws to the highest unit, to the smallest to the largest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who appoints commanders, assistants and deputies in the particular staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: This is regulated by the law on defence, and so in that regard the presidency has its own authority, the Supreme Command has its own authority, the main staff of the Federation Army has its own authority and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the chief of staff appoint his assistants and deputies, is he -- does he have authority to appoint the subordinate officers within his staff, or who appoints them?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: It is the commander or the -- or the competent command, but the whole staff can propose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can the commander -- can the chief of staff appoint his own -- can the chief of staff appoint his own deputies or assistants?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: No, he cannot. This is all in the rules. It depends on the level of the command. And this is also provided for in the law on defence. It is who can appoint whom, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the MUP was part, that MUP formations were part of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina. You testified to that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do these general principles on command and control are applicable to the MUP, in your view, to the MUP as part of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: That's not in my experience. It's so by law. And I must say that I have not, I have not studied this very closely. But the general rules, the general principles are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any questions, Ms. McMurrey?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence of Esad Landzo has no questions for the Brigadier. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Questions from the Prosecution? Cross-examined by Mr. Niemann

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, the order that you received on the 14th of April to go to the Konjic region and to prepare and organise the Territorial Defence, was an order that was signed by Hasan Efendic, the commander of the republican territorial headquarters, Jerko Doko, the minister of defence, and the president of the presidency, who, I assume, is President Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, of those gentlemen, Hasan Efendic is a military person, he has military rank and title, is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, he's the commander in chief of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the minister of defence, Jerko Doko, is he a military person or a civilian?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: At the relevant time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the relevant time.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: He is a civilian. And this is civilian leadership. And through new regulations, the ministry of defence has the regional staff and then under them were the municipal staff. This was the line of command and control at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think you'll agree with me that President Izetbegovic at the time was definitely civilian?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: President Izetbegovic was under one function, a civilian. But under another one, namely, the president and the presidency were the supreme command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I take it that the civilian representatives that signed and namely the minister for defence and President Izetbegovic, because they are civilians, they are signing merely as witnesses to the order signed by Hasan Efendic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. They were civilians, but under the law, one was a supreme commander of all armed forces and the other was head of the defence ministry which controlled all armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, and we've heard substantial evidence on a municipal level, Your Honours, but when a civilian signed, they did sign merely as witnesses and that the military signature was the one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The supreme commander under the constitution. For example, the President of Pakistan is supreme commander, he's not a military person. And the minister of defence, he's not a military person.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will be making an argument in due course, Your Honours, that the position on the municipal level operated in a similar way to the position on the republican level. And that's the import of my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I believe this is an incorrect question. This witness stated the legislation and regulation stating the authority and duties of military personnel and such regulation compared to the municipal level does not exist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I give an additional explanation? Concerning the municipal level --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Excuse me, there are periods of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: And there are periods for submission of arguments. And I think we can leave this for that period because this is not what the witness may be able to conclude it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have to base my submissions on something, Your Honours. I can't just do it out of the air. Just picking up on the objection from Ms. Residovic, it's difficult for me to conduct cross-examination when she objects to things merely because they are questions that she doesn't like to hear. If there's good foundation for the objection, well and good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I have indicated it's a necessary to objection to a matter which will finally come under submissions. The questions will be asked, then there answered. And then the conclusions will be left for final submissions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to Konjic, you met with Dr. Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic, who was president of the war presidency, that's right, isn't it?--

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, he was the president of the war presidency, but he had a civilian function because by the new regulation, municipal staffs were put outside of the war presidency and connected to district secretariats. So the commanders of municipal staff were not members of the war presidency. This is a very important regulation provision that was new at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps if you just answer my questions, we'll get over this process a lot faster. Now, when you went to Konjic, you went there with the express purpose of assisting and an advising in the organisation of the Konjic Territorial Defence, didn't you? A simple yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Absolutely yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would you see a member of the civilian leadership if that was your task and purpose?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: This is a well founded question. I meant to find out the information of the general situation in Konjic. I came to an unfamiliar territory and never had any official duties, nor friends, so I just wanted the know the information that were of my concern.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you known Dr. Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic, the president of the war presidency prior to this date?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: No, never. I have stated that yesterday. I did not know anybody in Konjic, neither civilians, nor the military personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now when you first met Mr. Delalic in Konjic, when you went there, were you aware that he had been given certain authorities, like yourself, by the minister of defence, Jerko Doko?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: No, I was not familiar with that, but he could have been given.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you would agree with me that, or you would state that Jerko Doko had authority or could give military functions to anyone in the Republic if he wanted to, couldn't he?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: No. Jerko Doko is a defence minister under his authority. His authorities are various, but under his authority he can appoint and the most common case was sending people to different countries in order to purchase supplies and equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he had the authority to permit you to carry out certain functions in the Konjic area, but when it came to Mr. Delalic, he lacked that authority, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: No. I said that under his authority he could have and he did. My order was signed by the commander of the TO and the minister of the defence and the president of the presidency. I could not go otherwise to Konjic. And the conditions for my arrival, physical arrival through the shortest routes to Konjic were non-existent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, a moment ago you told me that the minister of defence and the president of the presidency, because of their position and function, could give you a military direction and you're now saying something different.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: No, I am saying the same thing. Under the constitution and the law, the President of Bosnia and Herzegovina is a supreme command authority of all the armed forces, so all the orders connected to that level, they can obtain. This is under the constitution. The minister of defence has its own authority and everything falling within the scope of it, regardless whether this is a military or some other nature, he can perform, but within the framework of his authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Even now the minister of defence can do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the order that was given to you, was an order that could have been given by Mr. Efendic on his own or Mr. Doko on his own or President Izetbegovic on his own, couldn't he?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Not on his own for several reasons. It was jointly signed for a reason of Bosnia-Herzegovina being a internationally recognised state. To see that this is not a state of only one nationality, but a multi-ethnic state with its government, the presidency and other authorities, the nature, the multi-ethnic nature of the command of the authorities and all the governmental bodies, we needed to reconcile certain political aims at a time. It wasn't of my concern, but this was yet another reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is this provided for, because you had to cover all the multi-ethnic groups that everyone had to sign it before it became a valid order?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: This is a practice that's been kept up even today. A commander of the supreme command was Rasim Delic and even today I can bring you similar orders. That was valid for the period of transition of three years until we established joint command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you had received this order to go to Konjic and assist with the organisation of the Territorial Defence, it would have only been signed, say, for example, Hasan Efendic, you would have just ignored that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I haven't given a thought to it. I don't know if -- I probably would not ignore that as a soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about if you'd received it from President Izetbegovic, would you have ignored that one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He's said --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour..

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He's said that as a supreme commander of the armed forces, how can ignore the order of the supreme commander?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, he also said that everybody had to sign it in order to meet some multi-ethnic requirement about all being signed on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Maybe it was in accordance with the rules of that state.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, that's what I am asking, Your Honour. I am trying to explore that. Because there has been a lot of evidence here. For example, the president of the war presidency, and one would think that the a war presidency would have some relevancy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You're assuming that the federal set-up was duplicated at the municipal level.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We don't know that and we're trying to explore that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Please do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if it only came from one of them, you would have to assess your position according to who it was, is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: At the top level, the president of the presidency, the presidency and the supreme command are clearly defined. And anything below that, as the Honourable Judge stated, had to oblige under the orders. How can I stand against the supreme command? This was only at that level and the level of the ministry of defence. At all other levels, civilian authorities had no authority within the chain of command and control. This is regulated by the law. It's not an invention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, in hindsight it's easy to look back and see the way all this evolved, is it not? And then to say, well, this person had this authority and that person had that authority. But in reality, you were in Sarajevo, you were in Konjic, you're not seriously suggesting that the very fine letter of the law was applied while Sarajevo was fighting for its life, were you? You're not seriously suggesting that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Even at times of peace, you cannot really implement every single letter of the law, particularly not during the war. But in Konjic, where I was, nobody can say that the authorities there were not functioning as well as the system of command and control at the municipal level because it did at everybody's satisfaction. The HVO and the TO performed its tasks and the authorities were functioning. Under the conditions it may have been even ideal. But, as I said, there's in ideal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now when you went to Konjic to assist in the organisation of the Territorial Defence, did you ever tell any one or instruct any one that it would be helpful if civilians also signed military orders along with military personnel?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: No, I have not. I don't know why I would say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I might ask you why you wouldn't say that. Is there a reason why you wouldn't say that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I have seen a document shown to me yesterday. And if I remember correctly this was the May 18th. And a whole line of binding orders were concluded at the meeting of the war presidency and it was signed by the president of the war presidency together with the members, in order to harmonise the authorities of civilian and military authorities. And that it be controlled at that level to know whose competence is what. But there were instances if I need to go somewhere. Since the situation being as it was, I could not go from Jablanica to Mostar or from Konjic, unless I was given a permit from the HVO authority. So I cannot say that, for example, I needed an example of Ivica Azinovic or Petrovic and then the president and then the commander and then some additional people, only to make it legal to go through the control point, not to be returned or somebody might think that I deserted the army. My task was to do what I was tasked with, but instances were such in practice that there were permits or orders with three or four various people and one list, people of various structures and levels. But this is only when we talk about authorisations for supply or to get permission for a task to get equipment, ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Signing it in an official capacity, exercising authority, notwithstanding it might be for a limited purpose?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, is fine.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: Civilian wrote that for me to go through points more easily, to see that it is legal. I wish it were not so, but this is what was necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you said in your statement that you gave to Madam Residovic, that when you arrived in Konjic and until the 20th of May, Zejnil Delalic didn't hold any military post and that he dealt exclusively with logistical problems as such. You'd agree with me that logistics is a fundamental component of a military operation or an army, isn't it? It's a fundamental part of an army?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC.
utterances.text: I have to agree on the importance of logistics for any military operation. Maybe 70 per cent of the resources are engaged for the needs of logistics in modern armies, this is true. But for that purpose, we would engage people who never were military professionals. In our situation, these were people who were successful managers, business people, prominent people of the community and we used those people for those purposes. I have never heard before of Mr. Zejnil Delalic. I have just met him then, together with all the other people. And people expected that from those people, from those people who knew their way about good organisers because a municipality had to provide with medical aid, food, supplies needed for both civilians and the army and the process went parallel. Authorities would purchase equipment and supplies and sometimes there were people from command units doing so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in doing, in most armies, the role and function of logistics has devoted to it a whole chain of command going right up to the level of general in most instances, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Are you not pushing this interpretation too far? If a person is appointed to go between two persons and is now described as logistics, it doesn't really mean it conforms to the general approach of logistics in a normal army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As long as Your Honours have not been swayed by suggestions put to you that logistics is some sort of civilian function carried on by someone totally unconnected --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The army was so described, his function was a coordinator before he had a proper ability appointment, he was a coordinator.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The witness said he dealt exclusively with logistic problems and that's what I have dealt with in my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Dr. Hadzihuseinovic, who appointed him and explained what he appointed him for.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: He was a civilian and didn't appoint him to any military function. This witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Somebody who can assist you in getting the supplies. You mean without being inducted into the army, he can be given that function if that's more convenient.
